title: 1D Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem via IVT
description: Proves the 1D Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem: any continuous self-map of [0,1] has a fixed point. The key insight is that in dimension 1, Brouwer is equivalent to the Intermediate Value Theorem applied to f - id. Also proves uniqueness and geometric convergence for contractive maps. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Uses isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂ and tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one.

overview.historicalContext:
Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer (1881–1966) proved his celebrated fixed point theorem in 1911, publishing it in *Mathematische Annalen*. The result — that any continuous self-map of the $n$-dimensional ball $B^n$ has a fixed point — revolutionized topology and led directly to the development of degree theory and the concept of winding numbers.

In dimension 1, the result predates Brouwer entirely: it is a direct consequence of Bolzano's Intermediate Value Theorem (1817). For $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ continuous, consider $g(x)=f(x)-x$; then $g(0)=f(0)\geq 0$ and $g(1)=f(1)-1\leq 0$, so by IVT some $c$ satisfies $g(c)=0$, i.e., $f(c)=c$. The Lean proof avoids forming this auxiliary function by using `isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂` (the comparison form of IVT) directly with $f$ and $\text{id}$.

The **Banach Contraction Principle** (Stefan Banach, 1922), formalized in Part II-III of this file, strengthens the picture for contractive maps: when the Lipschitz constant $L < 1$, the fixed point is unique and the iterates $f^n(x_0)$ converge geometrically at rate $L^n$. This is the constructive backbone behind many numerical algorithms (fixed-point iteration, Newton's method for contractive systems).

The parent proof SpernerNDimOQ03.lean handles the general $n$-dimensional case via a displacement coloring argument based on Sperner's lemma — this 1D file provides the clean base case showing that dimension 1 is special: no Sperner machinery is needed.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-03-OQ-01)**: Can the Sperner-Brouwer pipeline be completed with the 1D base case, connecting it to the IVT?

**Answer: YES.** The 1D Brouwer theorem is a direct corollary of Mathlib's `isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂`. Combined with the n-D Sperner machinery from OQ-03, this provides a complete combinatorial path to Brouwer's fixed point theorem.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Step 1 (1D Brouwer):** Apply `isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂` with `g = id` and `f`: find c ∈ [0,1] where id(c) = f(c) using g(0) = id(0) ≤ f(0) and f(1) ≤ id(1) = 1.

**Step 2 (Uniqueness):** If f(x) = x and f(y) = y with L < 1, then |x - y| = |f(x) - f(y)| ≤ L|x - y|, so |x - y| = 0.

**Step 3 (Convergence):** By induction, |f^n(x₀) - p| ≤ L^n |x₀ - p|. Since L^n → 0, `tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one` gives geometric convergence.
keyInsights: In 1D, Brouwer is exactly IVT: apply intermediate_value₂ with id and f, using id(0)≤f(0) and f(1)≤id(1).
Mathlib's isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂ handles the comparison f ≥ g case directly — no auxiliary g(x) = f(x) - x needed.
Contractive convergence uses tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one for the geometric bound L^n → 0.
The n-D case (in OQ-03) requires Sperner's lemma and displacement coloring — IVT doesn't generalize directly.
This serves as the dimension-1 entry point of the Sperner-to-Brouwer pipeline proved in SpernerNDimOQ03.lean.
prerequisites: sperner-ndim-oq-03 (n-D Brouwer via Sperner, the parent open question)
isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂ in Mathlib (IVT for pairs of functions)

sections.title: Preamble: Dimension Gap and File Structure
sections.summary: Module comment explaining why IVT suffices in 1D but not n-D. Also imports and variable declarations for the contractive map theorems.
sections.mathContext: Why IVT works for $n=1$: $[0,1]$ is totally ordered, so boundary conditions $f(0)\geq 0$ and $f(1)\leq 1$ force a crossing. For $n>1$, the boundary $\partial[0,1]^n$ is not totally ordered — Sperner's lemma provides the combinatorial substitute.

sections.title: Part I: 1D Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem
sections.summary: brouwer_1d: any continuous f:[0,1]→[0,1] has a fixed point. Proved via isPreconnected_Icc.intermediate_value₂ with id and f, using f(0)≥0 and f(1)≤1.
sections.mathContext: For $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ continuous, $\text{id}(0)=0\leq f(0)$ and $f(1)\leq 1=\text{id}(1)$, so IVT gives $c$ with $f(c)=c$.

sections.title: Part II: Uniqueness for Contractive Maps
sections.summary: contractive_fixed_point_unique: if f has Lipschitz constant < 1, it has at most one fixed point. Proof by contradiction using |x-y| ≤ L|x-y| with L<1.
sections.mathContext: If $f(x)=x$ and $f(y)=y$ and $L<1$, then $|x-y|=|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L|x-y|$, forcing $|x-y|=0$.

sections.title: Part III: Geometric Convergence of Iterates
sections.summary: contractive_iterate_converges: iterates f^n(x₀) converge to the fixed point p with geometric rate L^n. Uses tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one for the bound.

sections.title: Part IV: Sperner-Brouwer Pipeline Entry
sections.summary: pipeline_1d: alias of brouwer_1d as the dimension-1 entry point of the Sperner-to-Brouwer pipeline.
sections.mathContext: The 1D case is the base case of the Sperner pipeline; higher dimensions use displacement coloring from OQ-03.

conclusion.summary: The 1D Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem is proved in 3 lines via Mathlib's IVT infrastructure. Contractive map uniqueness and geometric convergence are also fully proved. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: This completes the 1D base case of the Sperner-to-Brouwer pipeline. The full n-D pipeline is: (1) sperner_ndim gives approximate fixed points, (2) OQ-03 converts these to exact fixed points via displacement coloring, (3) this file handles the 1D case directly via IVT as a sanity check and pipeline entry point.
openQuestions: Can the 2D Brouwer theorem be proved via IVT on a subdivision argument, avoiding the full Sperner machinery?
Does the contractive iteration converge in a uniform metric sense, giving a single rate for all starting points?
